text.p: Manchester United were crowned English premier league champions for the fourth time in five years on Tuesday as their two main rivals failed to extend the title race into the final weekend of the season.

Liverpool's 2-1 defeat at Wimbledon and Newcastle's goalless draw at West Ham ensured that United retained their title without kicking a ball, confirming their position as English soccer's 'team of the Nineties.'
United finished runners-up to Blackburn in 1994-95 but Alex Ferguson's team, whatever their failings in Europe, have otherwise reigned supreme in domestic league football.

After all the fuss surrounding Ferguson's attempts to have the league season extended, it was doubly ironic that their latest triumph should be sealed with two games to go while his players had their feet up.
Second-placed Liverpool needed to avoid defeat to stand any chance of staying in the hunt but paid the price for defensive slackness and wastefulness in front of goal at Selhurst Park.

They were two goals down after 53 minutes to headers from Wimbledon's Jason Euell and Dean Holdsworth but had several chances to secure a point after youngster Michael Owen had pulled a goal back in the 74th minute.
Their failure left Newcastle as the only side who could still catch United but this time Kenny Dalglish, manager of Blackburn in their title year, was unable to prevent red celebrations.
The Newcastle team he inherited from Kevin Keegan have shown more defensive spine but were unable to break down a West Ham side still involved in the relegation scramble.

Only a fine save prevented Alan Shearer from breaking the deadlock in the second half and an overhead kick from Faustino Asprilla also shaved the target. But West Ham were good overall value for their point.
Newcastle and United meet on Thursday at Old Trafford. Newcastle are still chasing second place, but United's fans can afford to bask in the glory of their 11th English league title.
Manager Ferguson preferred not to watch events unfold on television but was quick to pay tribute to his team.

"It does get better because the demands are greater," he said. "The great thing about it is that we've had the Champions' League to contend with but have managed to maintain our challenge in the league as well."
Former captain Steve Bruce commented: "They set the standards for everyone else to follow."
